## 固定收益市場主線

華府與德黑蘭釋出更多外交協商空間，油價大幅回落，帶動較長天期美國公債上漲；同時，科技公司重返債市，給予投資人可觀的發行讓利。10年期殖利率下降1.64個基點至4.9125%，30年期下降2.25個基點至5.2857%。不過，通膨補償的降幅大於名目殖利率，2年期殖利率反而微升。這次行情緩解的是能源衝擊，並非資金成本全面下降。

伊朗總統表示，最高領袖已授權政府推進談判，川普總統也稱協商有所進展，布蘭特原油因而下跌8.11%，收在每桶$104.23。外交前景改善卻未能挽救科技股：半導體股下跌3.37%，那斯達克100指數下跌1.39%。即使Oracle完成$100億債券發行、Alphabet籌得€60億，市場對人工智慧投資報酬的疑慮仍然突出。

借款人利用基準殖利率下降的機會融資，投資人則要求補償日益擴大的資金需求。Oracle本次最長天期債券的發行利差為美國公債加335個基點，Alphabet的歐元固定利率債券平均發行讓利接近24個基點。週一公布的美國數據互有強弱：ISM製造業表現優於預期，價格指數回落，營建支出卻大幅下降。收盤時，市場仍須區分能源降價、需求韌性與個別發行人的融資風險。

## 油價回落壓低通膨補償

油價跌勢逐步擴大。Axios稍早報導，川普希望在可能恢復攻擊伊朗前，給外交協商更多時間。隨後，伊朗總統Masoud Pezeshkian表示，最高領袖Mojtaba Khamenei已賦予政府額外談判權限。消息公布後，倫敦市場布蘭特原油跌幅擴大至約6%，來到每桶$106附近，至美國固定收益市場收盤又進一步下跌。

川普其後在華府向記者表示，伊朗希望達成協議，雙方有可能談成。被問及週二美國期中選舉後是否恢復軍事打擊時，他以嘴形作出否定回應。德黑蘭仍保留實質條件：伊朗官員表示，要讓荷姆茲海峽的能源運輸恢復順暢並重返正式談判，華府必須解除經濟封鎖。當日外交空間雖然擴大，封鎖仍是爭議的一部分。

西德州原油收跌7.55%，報每桶$96.26。兩大原油基準仍高於一個月前，西德州與布蘭特分別上漲7.64%與5.59%，但單日急跌已大幅削減近期漲幅。Bloomberg Markets Live策略師Michael Ball指出，在實體供應持續吃緊之外，地緣政治溢價的變動愈來愈主導油價最大幅度的波動。

另一組油輪追蹤數據提供了新的供應比較。依Bloomberg及能源分析公司彙整資料，沙烏地阿拉伯、阿拉伯聯合大公國、伊拉克與科威特10月合計出口增加10%，至每日1,553萬桶，大致回到年初水準。伊朗則受美國海軍封鎖影響，出口連續第二個月為零。其他主要阿拉伯出口國恢復供應，與伊朗原油持續被排除在外，是供應情勢中不同的兩面。

美國公債各天期走勢不一。2年期殖利率上升0.61個基點至4.5937%，5年期下降1.07個基點至4.7091%。2年與10年期利差收窄2.25個基點至31.88個基點，2年與30年期利差縮小2.86個基點至69.2個基點。當日能源壓力緩解，較長天期名目公債受惠程度高於短端。

10年期損益兩平通膨率下降4.14個基點至2.303%，降幅超過同天期TIPS實質殖利率上升的2.5個基點；實質殖利率來到2.6095%。這顯示，當日名目公債上漲是通膨補償降低所致，而非實質殖利率下滑。若看一個月的變化，情況則不同：10年期名目殖利率下降36.05個基點，其中實質殖利率下降29.95個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降6.1個基點。

30年期雖領漲週一行情，若與一週前相比，表現仍落後其他天期。其殖利率僅下降1.71個基點，2年與10年期則分別下降12.22與7.59個基點；30年期過去一個月共下降33.53個基點。週一殖利率曲線趨平，卻未抹去過去一週長期借款成本相對難以下降的格局。

美國製造業數據顯示活動增強，價格壓力則有所放緩。10月ISM製造業PMI由54.5升至55.5，超過市場預期的54.6。新訂單由55.3升至55.5，就業則由52.7降至52.4。因此，整體指數改善伴隨的是訂單小幅增加、就業分項轉弱，而非各項活動同步加速。

ISM價格指數由77.9降至75.2，低於市場預期的77，顯示工廠投入價格壓力仍高，但已有緩和。另一份標普全球製造業PMI終值則呈現相反的活動變化，由55.9降至54.9，低於預期的56。兩份調查的整體指數均高於50，但變動方向不同，製造業動能並不像較強的ISM總指數單獨呈現的那麼一致。

9月營建支出月減1.9%，遠遜於預期的增加0.4%；前月增幅修正為2%。這項衡量實際活動的獨立數據出現明顯逆轉。綜合來看，ISM擴張增強，同時伴隨營建轉弱、標普調查成長放慢，以及工廠價格壓力減輕，尚未顯示整體經濟需求朝單一方向變化。

風險資產並未全面因壓力緩解而上漲。標普500指數下跌0.51%至7,541.40，VIX上升8.91%至21.15。美元指數微跌0.09%至101.79，黃金期貨上漲1.48%至每盎司$3,956.60。科技股疲弱蓋過油價下跌對股市的利多，半導體指數過去一個月已下跌21.38%。從10月30日至11月2日，LQD與HYG市價分別下跌0.54%與0.70%。兩檔均於11月2日除息；加回每股$0.399950與$0.401391配息後，單日含息報酬分別為負0.15%與負0.18%。JNK市價下跌0.77%，加回$0.543598配息後含息報酬為負0.19%；EMB市價下跌0.29%，加回$0.403699配息後含息報酬為正0.15%。除息造成的市價下跌本身，不能直接視為信用條件惡化。

## AI借款人付出讓利重返融資市場

Oracle完成融資，讓募資計畫成為投資人需求的直接考驗。公司發行$100億債券，同時籌集等額股權資金；債券分為五券，期限介於3年至20年，最長券發行利差為美國公債加335個基點。債券訂單高峰約$380億，依Bloomberg計算，相對既有債券的發行讓利約30個基點。

這筆交易以實質讓利吸引大量需求。美國銀行同時主導股票與債券發行，股票發行在週一稍早也已超額認購。投資人與分析師預期，這可能是Oracle未來數年最後一次為AI擴張而新增舉債，此後發債將主要用於既有債務再融資。CreditSights分析師仍預估，公司在2027至2029年間將發行約$200億債券，償還到期債務。因此，公司先前宣布限制總債務成長，並不排除持續的再融資需求。

整體初級市場異常忙碌。週一共有17家公司進入美國投資等級債市，為9月8日以來最多，包括HCA Healthcare、L3Harris Technologies與GATX；Carrier Global則是2023年以來首次回歸。其他借款人還有Otis Worldwide、Cheniere Energy、AEP Transmission、Textron、Eastman Chemical及Hyatt。企業趕在期中選舉與週五就業報告前籌資，交易商原先預估本週發行量約$450億。

Columbia Threadneedle投資組合經理Ed Al-Hussainy認為，融資窗口主要來自10月初以來殖利率下降，以及聯準會按兵不動後利率波動降低。他表示，9月與10月初的波動曾使殖利率敏感型買盤暫時退場，而第三季財報中企業槓桿狀況未出現重大意外惡化，也有助企業重返市場。不過，他也擔心，各評級信用市場都難以消化AI融資的規模與速度。

基準殖利率下滑，壓低了整體融資成本，但投資人要求的信用溢價反而更高。美國高評級公司債平均殖利率週五約為5.79%，低於9月及10月初逾6%的水準；科技業投資等級債平均利差週五卻達108個基點，高於去年底的76個基點。Bloomberg統計，今年企業為AI投資在美國高評級債市借款已超過$3,300億。以較低殖利率再融資的吸引力，與承擔企業風險所要求的更高補償，同時存在。

Alphabet的歐元交易尤其清楚呈現這項差異。公司發行€60億、共七券債券，期限介於2年至19年，訂單超過€171億，需求集中在最長天期券。加上5月的€90億發行，依Bloomberg比較，Alphabet的單一曆年歐元公司債發行量已超過Amazon在3月發行的€145億，成為最大發行人。

各券在建簿期間利差至少收窄20個基點，但公司付出的成本仍高於5月交易。2年期固定利率券利差訂為交換利率中間價加40個基點，19年期則為加185個基點。固定利率各券平均新券發行讓利接近24個基點，約為今年歐元公司債平均發行溢酬的三倍。Alphabet既有歐元債自發行以來利差最多擴大60個基點，加上整體公債遭拋售，也推高了新券必須提供的殖利率。

TwentyFour Asset Management投資組合經理Jack Daley強調Alphabet的資產負債表與既有歐元債Aa2評級，將公司的償債能力與令股市失望的業績表現區分開來。Rathbones的Bryn Jones則較審慎，希望先看到投資報酬的證據，或發債速度放慢，再加碼參與。雙方分歧在於持續資本需求應獲得多少補償，而不只是高評級發行人能否湊足訂單。

Meta正準備另一場大規模融資考驗。知情人士表示，公司考慮跨境發行至少$200億投資等級債券，尚未作出最終決定，規模也可能隨需求增加。花旗與摩根士丹利安排週一、週二舉行投資人電話會議。擬議美元券期限為5年至30年，歐元券則從略逾4年至略逾38年。若發行歐元券，將是Meta首次進入該市場；整筆交易也將是六個月來首次大型發債。

這項擬議債券融資之外，Meta也已進行或規劃股權籌資。公司上週完成$250億普通股定價，並以特別股籌得$125億，另規劃可再出售最多$600億股票的隨市價發行計畫。特別股資金已到位，隨市價發行計畫則提供未來售股管道；不同融資管道與進度共同顯示，資本需求不只落在債券投資人身上。

新加坡STT GDC正洽談S$31億、折合$24億聯貸，為旗下資產融資。知情人士表示，擬議貸款期限為3年，利率為新加坡隔夜平均利率加165個基點，並有最長延展2年的選擇權。渣打、大華銀行、華僑銀行與星展擔任全球統籌行、受委任主辦行及簿記行。165個基點是契約約定加在基準利率之上的利差，而非這筆擬議借款的完整利息成本。

最新營運揭露同時呈現融資需求背後的成長與支出。Anthropic第三季營收接近$170億，約為去年同期的十二倍，淨損則達$233億。營業費用增加292%至$175億；在準備首次公開發行之際，公司揭露未來數年擬投入超過$8,950億。營收快速擴張，伴隨的卻是更大虧損及龐大未來資金需求。

企業整併也有進展。Marvell同意以$1,150億企業價值收購Lumentum，從先前洽談推進至公布交易條件。這筆全股票交易將使Marvell股東持有合併後公司67%股權，並擴充連接AI晶片、伺服器與設施的光學技術。由於以股票支付，收購價值不能等同於新增現金借款需求。另外，Apple在盤後公布的9月季度營收年增12%至$1,145億，但成長放慢，中國銷售也低於預期。

## 資產出售入帳、債權保障與債券反彈

BP完成向Stonepeak出售Castrol的65%股權，取得$60億用於減債，讓已議定的資產處分轉為可供調整資產負債表的現金。BP第三季末淨債務為$138.7億，正在削減的其他負擔還包括混合資本工具、租賃及深水地平線事故和解款。執行長Meg O’Neill表示，交易帶來即時現金收入，同時保留參與Castrol未來成長的股權。

Cloud Software Group則以不同條件向債權人籌資，推出$20億優先擔保債券，為部分2029年到期債務再融資。這家獲Vista與Elliott支持、擁有Citrix及Tibco的公司，據知情人士透露，在條款中納入防範負債管理操作的保障。花旗與高盛、Vista主導交易，週一召開貸款人電話會議，預計週二定價。

投資人愈來愈懷疑軟體借款人抵禦AI競爭的能力，這些保障是吸引參與的重要條件。整體槓桿融資市場仍清淡：10月垃圾債發行量年減18%至$146億，槓桿貸款銷售量也較去年10月少逾10%。Cloud Software的擬議再融資一方面處理到期債務，一方面明訂債權保障，而非僅靠較低借款利率招徠投資人。

Acrisure新公布的營運數據緩解了市場對經紀業務留存率的疑慮，帶動次級市場債價強勁反彈。據知悉投資人更新內容的人士表示，北美零售業務留存率由第二季82.3%改善至第三季84.2%。2030年11月到期債券成交價約為面額87%，高於上週底約81%，以及三週前約73%。Trace數據顯示，週一美國高收益債漲幅最大的七檔證券中，有六檔來自Acrisure。

留存率改善，有助抵銷單季$1.31億現金淨流出的疑慮。調整後EBITDA為$3.36億，年減0.3%；營收$12.4億，有機成長率為負0.4%。先前，一份誤植於簡報的內部試算表曾引發留存率疑慮，公司在9月移除該表，要求投資人不要據此交易，並保留法律權利。這次數據讓債權人對營運表現有了更清楚的比較。

在資訊不明期間，市場曾出現放空，之後才迎來這波債券反彈。標普全球市場財智資料顯示，Acrisure規模$5.5億、2032年到期債券的放空部位上月激增。新留存率數據回應了公司業務重整期間的一項具體疑慮，但同時仍有現金流出、調整後獲利略降。因此，即使營運結果仍互有強弱，債價仍可能大幅回升。

## 央行重新評估持續的物價壓力

歐洲公債也隨債市上漲。Bloomberg市場報導顯示，德國10年期殖利率下降3個基點至3.29%，英國同天期下降9個基點至5.19%。不過，政策官員的評估未如當日能源行情所暗示的那麼寬鬆。斯洛伐克央行總裁Peter Kazimir週一警告，投資人可能低估了ECB為讓通膨重返目標並維持在該處，還需要進一步緊縮的幅度。

Kazimir著重壓力傳導的先後關係：能源價格較一年前高出近五分之一，企業成本上升，貨幣疲弱推升進口價格，食品價格也逐步走高。企業可能先累積成本，再轉嫁給消費者；而在更廣泛通膨出現之前，預期就可能改變。因此，單靠成長放慢未必足以壓低通膨。他談的是不只一場會議的政策路徑。

愛爾蘭央行總裁Gabriel Makhlouf的立場更具條件性，表示後續行動取決於下次會議前的數據，每次會議都可能採取行動。他另反對ECB立即介入支持法國債券，認為法國面臨的是財政問題，應由該國政治人物解決。這項最新表態把調整責任放在政府，而非以貨幣政策為財政難題提供後盾。

英國的政策辯論不只涉及昂貴能源能持續多久，也愈來愈關注需要多高利率才能抑制需求。Bloomberg在10月29至30日調查的35名經濟學家，全數預期英國央行將於11月5日升息0.25個百分點至4%。近60%預期票數為7比2，另有24%預期6比3；9月則只有三名委員支持升息。經濟學家也預期，央行將上修今年與明年的通膨預測、上修2026年成長預測，並下修失業率預測。

支持較高中性利率的理由，部分來自投資需求。截至8月的三個月，英國產出成長0.7%，失業率降至4.7%，雇主在9月增加1.3萬個職位。前英國央行決策官員Jan Vlieghe估計，中性利率約3.5%，並主張能源仍昂貴時，政策利率需達4.5%。央行上月市場參與者調查的中性利率平均估值為3.25%；Pantheon Macroeconomics的Rob Wood則引述里奇蒙聯準銀行模型，認為可能為3.75%，甚至更高。這些是對無法直接觀察之利率的不同估計，並非政策承諾。

新研究也挑戰英國借款成本上升純粹來自暫時性能源衝擊的解釋。英國國家經濟社會研究院（NIESR）將今年基準殖利率漲幅逾半歸因於AI投資熱潮及投資人要求更高溢價，僅40%直接來自中東能源成本。院長David Aikman表示，這意味利率可能持續偏高。油價回落可以降低眼前通膨壓力，卻未必逆轉支撐借款成本的資本需求。

日本央行完整季度展望則提出另一個衡量需求的角度。央行指出，人口減少加速，使整體消費愈來愈難出現強勁成長，即使個別家庭需求未惡化也是如此。今年初人均消費約比2015年高4%，整體消費卻幾乎持平。截至2025年的五年間，日本人口減少2.5%，是可追溯至1920年的紀錄中最大降幅。消費約占經濟一半，在央行考慮市場普遍預期的12月再度升息之際，這項分析影響對消費的判斷。

印度對油價下跌的反應更為直接。基準10年期殖利率盤中最多下降10個基點至7.32%，為5月初以來最大跌幅；5年期隔夜指數交換利率最多下降8個基點。Karur Vysya Bank財資主管VRC Reddy表示，若原油持續下跌，市場對印度央行12月升息幅度的預期可能由50個基點降至25個基點。他也指出，10月債市遭拋售後，較高殖利率吸引買盤；若油價繼續跌，未來幾天10年期殖利率可能來到7.25%。

巴基斯坦最新CPI顯示通膨放緩，但仍高於目標。10月物價年增9.6%，低於9月的10.26%，卻高於經濟學家預估中位數9.5%，也超過央行5%至7%的目標區間。食品通膨由8.2%降至7.74%，住宅與能源通膨由12.39%降至11.03%。Bloomberg Economics的Ankur Shukla預期，通膨將維持在10%附近至3月，於截至6月的季度回到目標區間，並認為12%的政策利率已具足夠限制性，可讓央行維持利率不變。

智利投資人調查顯示，通膨保障需求仍強。上週受訪的18名分析師與交易員中，近90%偏好UF通膨連結債，勝過披索債，是2025年3月恢復調查以來最高比例。約78%偏好1至5年期，近45%預期通膨連結債殖利率將在未來一個月下降。豐業銀行經濟學家預測11月通膨升至5%；巴克萊則假設2027年上半年油價約$110，預期通膨至3月仍接近5%。這些預測取決於能源與國內復甦情況，並未將週一油價下跌視為永久轉變。

## 主權融資與能源資金配置分歧

羅馬尼亞歷經逾五個月政治動盪後，重返國際債市，完成€45億、三券歐元債定價，訂單高峰超過€85億。這是5月聯合政府垮台、新政府獲批准後的首次發行。上週預算檢討維持赤字占GDP 6.2%的目標，同時騰出更多醫療資金。

財政部長Alexandru Nazare承諾維持財政紀律，以免評級遭降至投機等級。央行理事Cristian Popa週一警告，不應採取無法持續的支出擴張，並表示必須繼續削減赤字，才能避免融資困難。此次完成發行顯示新政府已能取得融資，而維持這項能力仍仰賴財政承諾。

波蘭面臨更迫近的制度期限。央行理事Adam Lipinski任期於11月4日屆滿，若未補上空缺，扣除總裁後的理事人數將低於法定最低六人。四名提名人正等待總理Donald Tusk批准，但Tusk與總裁Adam Glapinski及總統Karol Nawrocki之間存在爭議。法律專家對後果看法不一：Maciej Gutowski認為，理論上人數不足的理事會仍可履行職務，但其決議日後可能遭政治動機驅使的挑戰。

國會另推動將Glapinski送交國家法庭審理，也仍有爭議。Glapinski否認不當行為；憲法法庭已將所需表決門檻提高至國會席次的60%，超出執政聯盟單獨可達成的票數，並裁定不得依現行規則將其停職。波蘭基準公債相對德債的利差約300個基點，較8月擴大近三分之一，財政赤字則約占GDP 7%。迫近的理事空缺，為原已困難的財政環境增添具體運作不確定性。

日本完成¥2,500億氣候轉型債標售，最高得標殖利率為2.2%。投標倍數3.84倍，低於5月的4.62倍，但略高於2024年2月開始發行以來平均3.79倍。這是今年第五次、累計第十一次標售，屬於延續至2033年的¥150兆計畫。日本已以此名義發行超過$300億債券，主要由日本央行與國內機構買進。

資金用途仍有爭議。依日本信用評等機構資料，本會計年度合格項目涵蓋AI、半導體、機器人與核能技術，只有4%指定用於使再生能源成為主要電力來源。政府一面釋出戰略石油儲備、一面尋求更多元供應，環保團體則批評日本再度依賴化石燃料進口。日本目標是在2035會計年度，將排放較2013年減少60%；去年化石燃料仍占能源供應逾80%。

更廣泛的融資研究也呈現不均衡的轉型。Bloomberg估計，銀行今年來自氣候相關債券與貸款的收入約$30億，略高於石油、天然氣與煤炭債務的$29億，綠色債務手續費收入連續第五年居前。BloombergNEF另計算的能源供應銀行融資比率，2025年由2024年的0.95升至0.97，但其估計要達成氣候目標，2030年需達4比1。歐洲為2.5比1，中國為1.6比1，北美則降至0.5比1。綠色融資收入增加的同時，實際資本配置仍存在重大區域差異。

## 後續市場焦點

11月3日美國期中選舉到來前，企業已加快發債，股市波動也在升高。民主黨需在參議院淨增四席、眾議院淨增三席，才能分別取得多數；接近的選戰可能需數天甚至數週才能確定結果。政策焦點包括資料中心開發環境，以及下屆國會面臨的財政決策。總統否決權與可能的分裂政府，意味最終立法走向不只取決於最初席次結果。

在長端公債當日表現領先之後，美國財政部11月4日的季度再融資公告將交代發債期限配置。交易商對於是否立即縮減長債標售規模，或僅修改指引以容許日後調整，仍有分歧。若規模不變，下次再融資總額將為$1,250億：11月9日標售$580億3年期債、11月10日標售$420億10年期債，以及11月12日標售$250億30年期債。政府持續需要借款，未定之處在於如何分配至各期限。

製造業數據互有強弱之後，勞動與訂單數據將檢驗需求的廣度。9月JOLTS職缺將於11月3日UTC時間15:00公布，市場預期713萬個，前值707.9萬個；自願離職數據則提供另一個勞工流動性指標。同時公布的工廠訂單預期增加1.2%，前值增加0.1%。11月4日UTC時間13:15公布的ADP就業預期增加6.5萬人，前值9萬人。週五官方非農就業預測同樣增加6.5萬人，失業率預期維持4.2%，但民間與官方數據涵蓋的就業群體不同。

經濟學家一致預期英國央行升息，11月5日決議的焦點將是表決票數、修正預測與後續升息指引。ING的James Smith預期，英國央行仍會明確表示，後續行動取決於經濟。在日本，11月16日GDP將公布消費數據，法國巴黎銀行與第一生命經濟研究所預期消費下滑，之後才是日本央行12月18日決議。央行最新人口分析，使整體與人均需求的差異格外值得留意。

南非週三地方選舉是另一項主權風險考驗。William Blair的Yvette Babb認為，市場已預期民族團結政府維持穩定，因此維持現狀的結果可帶來的上行空間有限；若結果提高聯合政府失穩的可能性，反應可能更大。民主聯盟（DA）若增加支持，可強化偏向改革的聯盟；若經濟自由鬥士黨（EFF）與民族之矛黨（MK）侵蝕非洲民族議會（ANC）的支持，而DA未增強，則可能削弱聯盟。這些情境關乎財政政策能否延續，而非單一地方政府的選舉結果。

信用投資人也即將面對交易決策。Meta的電話會議週二繼續，Cloud Software的擔保再融資預計同日定價。兩者條件將顯示，債權人如何區分龐大的投資等級融資需求，與槓桿軟體企業的再融資及法律保障。在歐洲，美國證管會週一截止的諮詢，若最終採納擬議豁免，可能擴大美國投資人參與歐盟債券期貨的管道。Eurex過去20個交易日平均成交量僅略逾40口，改善避險管道對歐盟深化債市的努力因而相當重要。

英國首相Andy Burnham預定在週二於安地卡及巴布達舉行的高峰會，向較貧窮的英聯邦成員提出債務改革方案，尋求延長還款期限、提供更優惠利率，並爭取非G7援助國與私人債權人支持。他的辦公室表示，陷入債務困境的開發中國家約有一半屬於英聯邦。這仍是擬議架構，適用範圍取決於債權人參與。

能源仍是串連上述決策、眼前尚未解決的條件。德黑蘭取得新談判授權的同時，仍要求解除封鎖；其他波斯灣產油國出口恢復，則已增加可用供應。外交能否維持週一油價跌勢，將影響能源降價多快反映在通膨指標，以及央行判斷還需進一步緊縮多少。

overall_summary.headline: 油價回落壓低通膨補償，帶動較長天期美債上漲
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國與伊朗重啟談判的空間擴大，布蘭特原油下跌8.11%至每桶$104.23，帶動較長天期美國公債走高。10年期殖利率下降1.64個基點至4.9125%，30年期下降2.25個基點至5.2857%，2年期則上升0.61個基點至4.5937%。這波債市漲勢反映通膨補償下降：10年期損益兩平通膨率下降4.14個基點至2.303%，抵銷同天期實質殖利率上升2.5個基點至2.6095%的影響。

科技借款人以較高成本重新取得市場融資。Oracle完成$100億債券發行，最長券利差為美國公債加335個基點；Alphabet籌得€60億，固定利率各券平均發行讓利接近24個基點。Meta則考慮至少$200億的跨境債券發行，尚未定案。科技股下跌、股市波動升高之際，AI融資需求仍然龐大。

美國活動數據互有強弱：ISM製造業指數升至55.5，價格指數降至75.2，營建支出卻下降1.9%。伊朗要求美國解除封鎖的爭議仍未解決，能源價格能否持續降低，依然是通膨前景的關鍵。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

A sharp retreat in oil prices helped longer Treasuries advance as Washington and Tehran signaled more room for diplomacy, while technology companies returned to debt markets with substantial concessions to investors. The 10-year yield fell 1.64 basis points to 4.9125% and the 30-year declined 2.25 basis points to 5.2857%. Inflation compensation fell more than nominal yields, however, and the two-year yield edged higher: the session offered relief from the energy shock rather than a broad reduction in the cost of money.

Brent dropped 8.11% to $104.23 a barrel after Iran's president said the supreme leader had authorized the government to pursue negotiations and President Donald Trump indicated progress. The improvement in the diplomatic outlook did not rescue technology shares. Semiconductor stocks fell 3.37%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.39%, and doubts about the returns on artificial-intelligence spending remained prominent even as Oracle completed a $10 billion bond sale and Alphabet raised €6 billion.

Borrowers were taking advantage of lower underlying yields, but investors demanded compensation for the growing financing requirement. Oracle's longest new bonds priced 335 basis points over Treasuries, and Alphabet offered an average concession of nearly 24 basis points on its fixed-rate euro debt. Across the economy, Monday's releases were mixed: ISM manufacturing strengthened beyond expectations, its prices index moderated, and construction spending fell sharply. That combination left the distinction between cheaper energy, resilient demand and issuer-specific financing risk central to the close.

## Oil Relief Lowers Inflation Compensation

The oil decline developed in stages. Early reporting from Axios said Trump wanted to allow more time for diplomacy before potentially resuming strikes on Iran. Later, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had granted the government additional powers to negotiate. Brent's losses deepened to about 6% near $106 a barrel in London after that announcement, before extending further by the U.S. fixed-income close.

Trump subsequently told reporters in Washington that Iran wanted an agreement and one could happen. Asked whether he would resume military strikes after Tuesday's U.S. midterms, he mouthed a negative response. Tehran nevertheless retained a substantive condition: Iranian officials said easing energy transport through the Strait of Hormuz and returning to formal negotiations required Washington to lift its economic blockade. The day's change was a wider diplomatic opening, with the blockade still part of the dispute.

WTI finished down 7.55% at $96.26 a barrel. Both crude benchmarks remained above their month-earlier levels, with WTI up 7.64% and Brent 5.59%, but the daily fall substantially reduced their recent gains. Bloomberg Markets Live strategist Michael Ball attributed the largest crude swings increasingly to changes in the geopolitical premium, alongside continuing physical tightness.

Separate tanker-tracking figures added a new supply comparison. Combined exports from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq and Kuwait rose 10% in October to 15.53 million barrels a day, roughly matching volumes at the start of the year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg and energy-analytics firms. Iran's exports remained at zero for a second month under the U.S. naval blockade. The recovery among other major Arab exporters and the continuing exclusion of Iranian barrels described different parts of the supply picture.

Treasuries responded unevenly across maturities. The two-year yield rose 0.61 basis point to 4.5937%, while the five-year fell 1.07 basis points to 4.7091%. The two- to 10-year curve flattened 2.25 basis points to 31.88 basis points, and the two- to 30-year gap narrowed 2.86 basis points to 69.2 basis points. Longer nominal debt benefited more than the short end from the day's relief.

At 10 years, the breakeven inflation rate fell 4.14 basis points to 2.303%, more than offsetting a 2.5-basis-point rise in the TIPS real yield to 2.6095%. That decomposition gives the nominal rally a specific character: lower inflation compensation, rather than lower real yields, accounted for the decline. Over the month, the balance remained different. The nominal 10-year yield was down 36.05 basis points, with the real yield 29.95 basis points lower and the breakeven down 6.1 basis points.

The longest maturity also continued to lag over the broader weekly comparison despite leading Monday's advance. The 30-year yield was only 1.71 basis points below its week-earlier level, against declines of 12.22 basis points at two years and 7.59 basis points at 10 years. Over the month, 30-year yields had fallen 33.53 basis points. Monday compressed the curve without erasing the greater resilience of long borrowing costs over the week.

U.S. manufacturing data supplied a firmer activity signal alongside some price moderation. October ISM Manufacturing PMI rose to 55.5 from 54.5, exceeding the 54.6 consensus. New orders increased to 55.5 from 55.3, while employment eased to 52.4 from 52.7. The headline improvement therefore came with a small increase in orders and a weaker employment component, rather than acceleration in every part of the survey.

The ISM prices index fell to 75.2 from 77.9, below the consensus expectation of 77. Factory input-price pressure moderated while remaining pronounced. The separate final S&P Global Manufacturing PMI moved the other way on activity, falling to 54.9 from 55.9 and undershooting expectations of 56. Both headline surveys remained above 50, but their changes differed, leaving a less uniform account of manufacturing momentum than the stronger ISM headline alone suggested.

September construction spending fell 1.9% on the month, against an expected 0.4% increase, following a revised 2% gain. That was a substantial reversal in a separate measure of realized activity. Together, the releases paired stronger ISM expansion with softer construction, slower S&P survey growth and reduced factory price pressure, rather than establishing a single direction for demand across the economy.

Risk assets did not deliver a broad relief rally. The S&P 500 declined 0.51% to 7,541.40 and the VIX rose 8.91% to 21.15. The Dollar Index slipped 0.09% to 101.79, while gold futures gained 1.48% to $3,956.60 an ounce. Technology weakness outweighed the benefit of cheaper oil for the equity benchmarks, with the semiconductor index down 21.38% over the month. In fixed-income funds, LQD and HYG prices fell 0.54% and 0.70%, respectively, from October 30 to November 2. Both went ex-distribution on November 2: adding the declared cash distributions of $0.399950 and $0.401391 gives one-day total returns of minus 0.15% and minus 0.18%, respectively. JNK fell 0.77% on price but returned minus 0.19% including its $0.543598 distribution; EMB fell 0.29% on price but returned plus 0.15% including its $0.403699 distribution. Ex-distribution price declines alone therefore do not measure a deterioration in credit conditions.

## AI Borrowers Pay for Renewed Market Access

Oracle's completed financing turned its fundraising plans into a direct test of investor demand. The company sold $10 billion of bonds alongside an equal amount of equity, with the debt divided into five tranches maturing in three to 20 years. The longest notes priced 335 basis points over Treasuries. Peak bond orders reached about $38 billion, and the company offered roughly 30 basis points above its existing debt, according to Bloomberg's calculation.

The transaction attracted substantial demand at a meaningful concession. Bank of America led both the stock and bond offerings, and demand for the equity sale had also exceeded the amount sought earlier Monday. Investors and analysts expected this could be Oracle's last new-debt offering for AI expansion for several years, with subsequent bond sales largely refinancing existing obligations. CreditSights analysts still anticipated around $20 billion of issuance in 2027-2029 to refinance maturities. That distinction leaves refinancing needs alongside the company's previously announced limit on gross debt growth.

The broader primary market was unusually busy. Seventeen companies entered the U.S. investment-grade market Monday, the longest lineup since September 8, including HCA Healthcare, L3Harris Technologies and GATX. Carrier Global returned for the first time since 2023. Other borrowers included Otis Worldwide, Cheniere Energy, AEP Transmission, Textron, Eastman Chemical and Hyatt. Dealers had expected roughly $45 billion of issuance for the week as companies sought funding before the midterms and Friday's employment report.

Columbia Threadneedle portfolio manager Ed Al-Hussainy attributed the window chiefly to lower yields since early October and reduced rate volatility after the Fed's hold. Yield-sensitive demand had temporarily stepped back during the September and early-October volatility, he said, while the absence of major negative leverage surprises in Q3 results helped companies return. His assessment of issuance conditions was accompanied by a broader concern that credit markets across ratings were struggling to absorb the scale and speed of AI financing.

Lower underlying yields have softened all-in costs even as investors demand larger credit premiums. The average U.S. high-grade corporate yield stood around 5.79% Friday after exceeding 6% in September and early October. Technology-sector investment-grade spreads, by contrast, averaged 108 basis points Friday, against 76 basis points at the end of last year. Companies had borrowed more than $330 billion in U.S. high-grade bonds for AI investments this year, according to Bloomberg. The attraction of refinancing at a lower yield coexisted with a higher price for corporate risk.

Alphabet's euro transaction made that separation especially clear. Its €6 billion sale comprised seven parts spanning two to 19 years, with orders above €17.1 billion and demand concentrated in the longest tranche. Together with May's €9 billion offering, the deal put Alphabet ahead of Amazon's €14.5 billion March sale as the largest corporate euro issuer in a calendar year in Bloomberg's comparison.

Spreads tightened at least 20 basis points across the tranches during book-building, but the company still paid more than at its May transaction. The two-year fixed-rate portion was set at 40 basis points over mid-swaps and the 19-year at 185 basis points. Across the fixed-rate bonds, the average new-issue concession was nearly 24 basis points, about three times the average euro corporate premium this year. Its existing euro bonds had widened as much as 60 basis points since issuance, while the wider government-bond selloff also increased the yields required on the new securities.

TwentyFour Asset Management portfolio manager Jack Daley emphasized Alphabet's balance sheet and the Aa2 rating on its existing euro bonds, distinguishing the company's credit capacity from the disappointment in its equity results. Rathbones' Bryn Jones was more cautious, wanting evidence of returns on investment or a slower issuance pace before becoming more involved. The disagreement concerned the compensation for continuing capital demands, not simply whether orders could be assembled for a highly rated issuer.

Meta was preparing another large test. People familiar with the discussions said it was considering at least $20 billion of cross-border investment-grade debt, with no final decision and the amount capable of increasing with demand. Citi and Morgan Stanley were arranging investor calls Monday and Tuesday. Proposed dollar maturities ranged from five to 30 years, while euro maturities ran from just over four to just over 38 years. A euro sale would be Meta's first, and the transaction its first major debt offering in six months.

The contemplated bonds sit beside equity financing already undertaken or planned. Meta priced $25 billion of common stock and raised $12.5 billion of preferred equity last week, and plans an at-the-market program allowing up to $60 billion of additional share sales. These are different funding channels and stages: the preferred financing had raised money, while the market-sale program provides a route to future issuance. Together they show how the capital requirement extends beyond bond investors.

In Singapore, STT GDC was discussing a S$3.1 billion, or $2.4 billion, syndicated loan to finance its assets. The proposed three-year facility carried a margin of 165 basis points over the Singapore Overnight Rate Average and an extension option of up to two years, according to people familiar with it. Standard Chartered, UOB, OCBC and DBS were working as global coordinators, mandated lead arrangers and bookrunners. The margin is the contractual addition to the benchmark, not the full interest cost of the prospective borrowing.

Fresh operating disclosures illustrated both the growth and expense behind the financing demand. Anthropic reported almost $17 billion of Q3 revenue, nearly twelve times the year-earlier amount, and a $23.3 billion net loss. Operating expenses rose 292% to $17.5 billion, and the company disclosed intended spending above $895 billion in the years ahead as it prepared for an IPO. Rapid revenue expansion therefore accompanied a larger loss and a substantial prospective funding requirement.

Corporate consolidation advanced as well. Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum at a $115 billion enterprise value, moving beyond the earlier negotiations to announced terms. The all-stock transaction would leave Marvell shareholders owning 67% of the combined business and expand its optical technology for connecting AI chips, servers and facilities. The form of consideration distinguishes the takeover value from an equivalent new cash-borrowing requirement. Meanwhile, Apple's September-quarter revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion, but growth slowed and China sales missed estimates in its late-hours release.

## Cash Proceeds, Creditor Protections and a Borrower Rebound

BP completed the sale of a 65% interest in Castrol to Stonepeak, delivering $6 billion for debt reduction. The closing converts an agreed disposal into cash available for the company's balance-sheet reset. BP reported net debt of $13.87 billion at the end of Q3; the obligations it is working to reduce also include hybrids, leases and Deepwater Horizon settlement payments. Chief Executive Meg O'Neill said the transaction brought immediate proceeds while preserving a stake in Castrol's future growth.

Cloud Software Group approached lenders from a different position, launching $2 billion of senior secured notes to refinance part of its debt due in 2029. The Vista- and Elliott-backed owner of Citrix and Tibco included protections against liability-management exercises, according to a person familiar with the offering. Citi led the transaction with Goldman Sachs and Vista, with a Monday lender call and pricing expected Tuesday.

The safeguards were part of the terms being offered to attract investors increasingly skeptical about software borrowers' resilience to AI competition. The wider leveraged-finance market remained quiet: October junk-bond issuance fell 18% from a year earlier to $14.6 billion, while leveraged-loan sales were more than 10% below the previous October. Cloud Software's proposed refinancing addresses maturities while specifying creditor protections, rather than relying only on a lower borrowing rate to secure participation.

Acrisure supplied a striking secondary-market reversal after new operating figures eased concern about broker retention. North American retail retention improved to 84.2% in Q3 from 82.3% in Q2, according to people familiar with its investor update. Its November 2030 bonds traded around 87 cents on the dollar, up from about 81 cents at the end of last week and roughly 73 cents three weeks earlier. Acrisure securities accounted for six of the seven largest gains across U.S. high yield Monday, according to Trace data.

The retention improvement helped offset $131 million of quarterly cash burn. Adjusted EBITDA was $336 million, down 0.3% from a year earlier, while revenue totaled $1.24 billion and organic growth was minus 0.4%. Those results gave creditors a clearer operating comparison after an internal spreadsheet mistakenly embedded in a presentation had raised doubts about retention. The company removed it in September and asked investors not to trade on the information, reserving its legal rights.

The bond rally followed short selling during the period of uncertainty. Short interest in Acrisure's $550 million of 2032 bonds surged last month, S&P Global Market Intelligence data showed. The new retention figures addressed a specific concern during a business overhaul; they arrived with continuing cash outflow and slightly lower adjusted earnings. That combination explains why a sharp price recovery could accompany operating results that were still mixed.

## Central Banks Reassess Persistent Price Pressure

European government bonds joined the advance in duration, with Bloomberg's market account showing Germany's 10-year yield down 3 basis points to 3.29% and Britain's down 9 basis points to 5.19%. Policymakers' assessments remained less accommodating than the day's energy move might suggest. Slovakia's Peter Kazimir warned Monday that investors could underestimate how much further ECB tightening would be needed to restore inflation to target and keep it there.

Kazimir focused on the sequence through which pressure can spread: energy was almost a fifth more expensive than a year earlier, companies faced higher costs, currency weakness increased import prices and food prices were edging up. Businesses could accumulate costs before passing them on, and expectations could change before broader inflation appeared. Slower growth alone might therefore be insufficient to bring inflation down. His argument concerned the path of policy beyond a single meeting.

Irish central-bank Governor Gabriel Makhlouf was more conditional, saying subsequent action would depend on the data before the next meeting and that every meeting remained live. He separately rejected immediate ECB intervention to support French debt, describing France's difficulties as a fiscal problem for its politicians to resolve. That fresh statement placed responsibility for adjustment with the government rather than offering a monetary backstop for the fiscal challenge.

Britain's policy debate increasingly concerns the interest rate required to restrain demand as well as the persistence of expensive energy. A Bloomberg survey conducted October 29-30 found all 35 economists expecting a quarter-point increase to 4% on November 5. Nearly 60% anticipated a 7-2 vote and another 24% a 6-3 split, compared with only three members favoring an increase in September. Economists also expected higher inflation forecasts for this year and next, stronger projected 2026 growth and lower unemployment.

The case for a higher neutral interest rate rests partly on investment. UK output rose 0.7% in the three months through August, unemployment fell to 4.7%, and employers added 13,000 jobs in September. Former BOE policymaker Jan Vlieghe estimated neutral around 3.5% and argued rates needed to be 4.5% while energy remained expensive. The BOE's market-participant survey last month put the average neutral estimate at 3.25%; Pantheon Macroeconomics' Rob Wood cited a Richmond Fed model suggesting 3.75%, possibly higher. These are different estimates of an unobserved rate, not policy commitments.

New research also challenged a purely temporary-energy explanation for UK borrowing costs. NIESR attributed more than half of this year's increase in benchmark yields to the AI investment boom and higher investor premiums, and only 40% directly to Middle East energy costs. Director David Aikman said that raised the possibility of persistently higher rates. The comparison leaves room for oil relief to lower immediate inflation pressure without reversing the demand for capital supporting borrowing costs.

The BOJ's full quarterly outlook supplied a distinct argument about demand measurement. It said the accelerating population decline made robust aggregate consumption growth increasingly difficult even without deterioration in individual household demand. Consumption per person early this year was roughly 4% above 2015, while aggregate consumption was almost flat. Japan's population fell 2.5% over the five years to 2025, its fastest recorded decline in figures going back to 1920. The analysis matters to the assessment of consumption, which accounts for about half the economy, as the bank considers another increase widely expected in December.

India showed a more immediate response to falling oil. Its benchmark 10-year yield declined as much as 10 basis points to 7.32%, the largest fall since early May, and five-year overnight-indexed swaps fell as much as 8 basis points. Karur Vysya Bank treasury head VRC Reddy said a sustained crude decline could reduce expectations for a December RBI increase from 50 to 25 basis points. He also reported buying interest at higher yields after October's selloff and envisaged 7.25% on the 10-year in coming days if oil kept falling.

Pakistan's new CPI reading showed moderation but continuing above-target inflation. October prices rose 9.6% from a year earlier, down from 10.26% in September but above the 9.5% economist median and the central bank's 5%-7% target band. Food inflation eased to 7.74% from 8.2%, and housing and energy inflation to 11.03% from 12.39%. Bloomberg Economics' Ankur Shukla expected inflation near 10% through March before returning to the target range in the quarter through June, and judged the 12% policy rate restrictive enough to allow a hold.

Chile's investor survey highlighted continuing demand for inflation protection. Almost 90% of 18 analysts and traders surveyed last week preferred UF inflation-linked bonds over peso debt, the strongest preference since the survey resumed in March 2025. Around 78% favored maturities of one to five years and almost 45% expected inflation-linked yields to fall over the next month. Scotiabank economists forecast inflation reaching 5% in November, while Barclays expected it near that rate through March under an assumption of oil around $110 in the first half of 2027. Those forecasts remained conditional on energy and domestic recovery rather than incorporating Monday's oil decline as a permanent change.

## Sovereign Access and Energy Financing Diverge

Romania returned to international bond markets after more than five months of political turmoil, pricing €4.5 billion across three euro tranches with peak orders above €8.5 billion. The sale was the first since approval of a new government, following the coalition collapse in May. Its budget review last week retained a 6.2%-of-GDP deficit target while freeing more money for healthcare.

Finance Minister Alexandru Nazare pledged fiscal discipline to avoid a downgrade to speculative grade. Central-bank board member Cristian Popa warned Monday against unsustainable spending increases and called further deficit reduction essential to avoiding funding complications. The completed issuance demonstrated access under the new administration; the fiscal commitments remain central to maintaining that access.

Poland faced a nearer institutional deadline. Central-bank board member Adam Lipinski's term expires November 4, and failure to fill the vacancy would leave membership excluding the governor below the legal minimum of six. Four nominees awaited Prime Minister Donald Tusk's approval amid his dispute with Governor Adam Glapinski and President Karol Nawrocki. Legal experts differed over the consequences: Maciej Gutowski said an incomplete board could in theory continue its duties, but decisions might later face politically motivated challenges.

The separate parliamentary effort to put Glapinski before a State Tribunal also remained disputed. He denied wrongdoing; the Constitutional Tribunal had raised the required voting threshold to 60% of seats, beyond the governing coalition alone, and had ruled against suspension under existing rules. Poland's benchmark premium over German debt was around 300 basis points, nearly a third wider since August, against a deficit around 7% of GDP. The impending board vacancy added a concrete operational uncertainty to an already difficult fiscal setting.

Japan completed a ¥250 billion climate-transition bond auction at a highest accepted yield of 2.2%. Bid-to-cover was 3.84, below May's 4.62 but slightly above the 3.79 average since issuance began in February 2024. It was the fifth sale this year and the eleventh overall, within a ¥150 trillion program through 2033. Japan has issued more than $30 billion under the designation, largely purchased by the BOJ and domestic institutions.

The allocation of proceeds remained contested. This fiscal year's eligible projects include AI, semiconductors, robotics and nuclear technologies, while only 4% is earmarked for making renewable energy a major power source, according to Japan Credit Rating Agency. Environmental groups criticized renewed reliance on fossil imports as the government released strategic oil reserves and sought more diverse sources of supply. The country's emissions target is a 60% reduction by fiscal 2035 from 2013 levels, while fossil fuels accounted for more than 80% of energy supply last year.

Broader financing research showed a similarly uneven transition. Bloomberg put bank revenue from climate-related bonds and loans at roughly $3 billion this year, slightly ahead of $2.9 billion from oil, gas and coal debt, marking a fifth consecutive year of higher green-debt fees. BloombergNEF's separate energy-supply banking ratio rose to 0.97 in 2025 from 0.95 in 2024, compared with the 4-to-1 ratio it estimates is needed by 2030 to meet climate goals. Europe reached 2.5 to 1 and China 1.6 to 1, while North America fell to 0.5 to 1. Higher green-financing revenue thus accompanied substantial regional differences in the underlying allocation of capital.

## Forward Market Significance

The November 3 U.S. midterms arrive with companies having accelerated issuance and equity volatility rising. Democrats need net gains of four Senate seats and three House seats for majorities, while close contests could take days or weeks to resolve. The relevant policy questions include the environment for data-center development and the fiscal decisions facing the next Congress. Presidential veto power and potentially divided government leave the eventual legislative response dependent on more than the initial seat count.

Treasury's November 4 refunding announcement will address the maturity mix after the long end's daily outperformance. Dealers remain divided over an immediate reduction in long-bond auctions versus a guidance change allowing later adjustments. If sizes remain unchanged, the next refunding would total $125 billion: $58 billion of three-year notes November 9, $42 billion of 10-year notes November 10 and $25 billion of 30-year bonds November 12. The outstanding question is how funding will be allocated across maturities, alongside the government's continuing borrowing requirement.

Labor and orders data will test the breadth of demand after the mixed manufacturing releases. September JOLTS openings are due November 3 at 15:00 UTC, with consensus at 7.13 million after 7.079 million; quits will add a separate measure of worker mobility. Factory orders at the same time are expected to rise 1.2% after 0.1%. November 4 ADP employment, due at 13:15 UTC, is expected to increase 65,000 after 90,000. Friday's official payroll forecast is also 65,000, with unemployment expected to remain 4.2%, but the private and government releases measure different employment populations.

Britain's November 5 rate decision will turn the unanimous economist expectation for a hike into a test of the vote, revised forecasts and guidance on further increases. ING's James Smith expects the BOE to keep subsequent action explicitly dependent on the economy. In Japan, November 16 GDP will bring the consumption figures that BNP Paribas and Daiichi Life Research Institute expect to show a decline, before the BOJ's December 18 decision. The bank's new demographic analysis makes the distinction between aggregate and per-person demand especially relevant.

South Africa's Wednesday municipal elections present a separate sovereign-risk test. William Blair's Yvette Babb sees limited upside from a status-quo result because stability of the Government of National Unity is already expected, but a larger potential response if the outcome raises the perceived likelihood of coalition instability. Gains for the Democratic Alliance could strengthen the reform-oriented coalition; gains for the EFF and MK at the ANC's expense, without a stronger DA, could undermine it. Those alternatives concern the durability of fiscal policy rather than the result in any one municipality.

Credit investors face imminent transaction decisions as well. Meta's calls continue Tuesday, and Cloud Software's secured refinancing is expected to price that day. Their terms will show how lenders distinguish very large investment-grade funding needs from leveraged-software refinancing and legal protections. In Europe, the SEC consultation that closed Monday could eventually broaden U.S. access to EU bond futures if the proposed exemption is adopted. Eurex turnover has averaged barely more than 40 contracts over 20 sessions, leaving improved hedging access important to the bloc's effort to deepen its debt market.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is due to propose debt reform for poorer Commonwealth members at Tuesday's summit in Antigua and Barbuda, seeking longer repayment periods and more favorable rates with support from non-G7 donor countries and private creditors. His office says about half the developing countries struggling with debt belong to the Commonwealth. The initiative remains a proposed framework whose reach depends on creditor participation.

Energy remains the immediate unresolved condition across these decisions. Tehran's demand for an end to the blockade stands alongside the new negotiating authority, while restored exports from other Gulf producers have increased available supply. Whether diplomacy sustains Monday's fall in crude will influence how quickly lower energy costs reach inflation measures and how much further central banks judge they must tighten.

All 35 economists surveyed expected a BOE increase to 4% on November 5 as the UK debate extended to higher neutral rates and investment demand. The BOJ distinguished resilient per-person consumption from weak aggregate growth; oil relief eased India's rate outlook, while Pakistan and Chile still faced persistent inflation.

section_summaries.section_title: Sovereign Access and Energy Financing Diverge
section_summaries.summary: Romania sold €4.5 billion of bonds after a prolonged absence, with fiscal discipline central to preserving access. Poland faced a November 4 central-bank board vacancy amid disputed legal consequences. Japan's ¥250 billion transition-bond auction drew lower demand than May's sale, while broader green-financing fee growth masked uneven regional capital allocation.

The midterms and Treasury refunding will clarify fiscal prospects and the maturity mix of borrowing. Labor releases and the BOE decision will test demand and persistent price pressure, while Meta and Cloud Software face financing decisions. Whether diplomacy sustains cheaper oil remains the immediate condition linking the inflation outlook to central banks' need for further tightening.

overall_summary.headline: Oil relief lifts longer Treasuries through lower inflation compensation
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Longer Treasuries advanced as renewed scope for U.S.-Iran negotiations sent Brent down 8.11% to $104.23 a barrel. The 10-year yield fell 1.64 basis points to 4.9125% and the 30-year declined 2.25 basis points to 5.2857%, while the two-year rose 0.61 basis point to 4.5937%. The rally reflected lower inflation compensation: the 10-year breakeven fell 4.14 basis points to 2.303%, outweighing a 2.5-basis-point rise in the real yield to 2.6095%.

Technology borrowers regained market access at a price. Oracle completed a $10 billion bond sale with its longest notes at 335 basis points over Treasuries; Alphabet raised €6 billion with an average concession of nearly 24 basis points on its fixed-rate bonds. Meta was considering at least $20 billion of cross-border debt, with no final decision. AI financing needs remained substantial even as technology shares fell and equity volatility rose.

U.S. activity releases were mixed: ISM manufacturing strengthened to 55.5 and its prices index eased to 75.2, but construction spending fell 1.9%. Iran's demand for an end to the U.S. blockade remained unresolved, leaving the persistence of cheaper energy central to the inflation outlook.
overall_summary.summary: A wider diplomatic opening between Washington and Tehran reduced the energy premium, while rising real yields and substantial concessions on AI-related debt kept the relief distinct from a broad decline in financing costs.
